heuristics.statement: The first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings and their chaining values cv = F_38(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values. Consequences used: within one chaining value the 2^26 table values F(a0) of window R = 9 behave as independent uniform words over the 2^23-bucket table of Appendix A.15, whose buckets are loaded in a uniform cyclic order and capped at seven lanes (H7), so a bucket holds E[min(Binomial(2^26, 2^-23), 7)] = 6.336269 filled lanes and the scan finds claws/u = 40 x 6.336269 x 4/512 = 1.980084 (20 row-16 heads x 2 windows; the four free low bits {0,1,4,5}); F7 has probability |F7|/2^32; the X_j and the online works W_j of different chaining values are independent (proof.md Lemma 3, Section 7).
heuristics.scope: The expected claw count 1.980084 per u, the mean online work wbar (hence V_MAX) of A.15.4, the independence used by Bernstein's inequality for the cap (proof.md Section 5, Lemmas 2 and 3) and the product over chaining values in the success bound (proof.md Section 7).
heuristics.extrapolation: Our C port (dev/claw/t7.c) at 2^25 slots loaded with the 2^26 candidates of window R = 9 measured occupancy 0.864763 to 0.864816 on four chaining values (formula 0.864665) and 1.07836 to 1.07917 claws per scanned word over 2^23 scan words each, against the formula 160 occ / 2^7 = 1.08100 (ratio 0.9976 to 0.9983); the parent's own port at 2^26 slots measured 0.63216 and 0.99898. The organizer experiment p1-online-r38 reports occupancy, claws, reference claws and expected claws on seed-drawn chaining values at a reduced table (ls = 16, 2^17 candidates). The scan words u0 + n are distinct and u0 is a fresh random word per chaining value, so the scan adds no dependence (proof.md Section 3).
heuristics.limitations: A premise, not a theorem: within each chaining value the table values F(a0), their tags and the claws found are taken to follow the per-chaining-value random-function law; independent first blocks do not by themselves prove it. The retained lanes of a bucket are the seven positions that follow a uniform rotation of the insertion order, i.e. an arc of seven rather than an arbitrary subset (H7); the score uses only that their tags are uniform, which retention does not condition on. Checked at reduced and full table size on a few chaining values, not on 2^54 of them.

heuristics.statement: For the claws the procedure finds, Pr[C1 and C2 and G and F7] = q_pf = 57,726,359,870,197 x 287,309,824 / 2^90 = 2^-16.1877, the rate enumerated exhaustively over all 2^32 words (P(C1) = 1/8, |C1 and C2| = 53,096,854, the window-R = 9 G count 57,726,359,870,197, |F7| = 287,309,824); the stage rates 1/8, 2^-6.3379, 2^-12.2857 set the mean post-filter cost.
heuristics.scope: The good pairs per chaining value (62,193.16) and the mean post-filter work in wbar (proof.md Sections 5, 6).
heuristics.extrapolation: Section 7 already takes E[K] over all 2^32 scan words, and this filing's ledger scans all 2^32 words u = u0 + n per chaining value, so the ledger and the probability analysis use the same scan. Our C port at n0 = 2^26 measured occupancy 0.63216 and claws/expected 0.99898 over 2^20 scan words; the organizer experiment p1-online-r38 reports occupancy, claws and expected claws on seed-drawn chaining values, and the scan words u0 + n are distinct with u0 a fresh random word per chaining value (proof.md Section 3).
heuristics.limitations: A premise that the exhaustive rates hold for the claws found; F7 is chaining-value dependent (measured heterogeneity 1.254).

heuristics.statement: A good pair is accepted by step 3b with probability q3r >= q3_P1 x 2^32 / 160 = 2^-71.4010, where q3_P1 = 2^-96.0791 = q3_model x 2^D_LB: q3_model = 2^-96.0133 is the registered accepted-event rate of the A0-variant good pairs on P8 before row 16 (row 16 has probability 160/2^32 and a P1 good pair has passed it) and D_LB = -0.0658 is the registered one-sided 99% lower bound of the paired per-seed difference L(P1) - L(A0) measured with the P1 law of this package's window (a0 in [9 x 2^26, 10 x 2^26) given G, a1 uniform on C1 and C2). This filing inherits the bound unchanged: the table retune does not touch q3, q3r, the relaxation ratio, the paired R9 run or any part of the transfer, and the identical bound (q3_model 2^-96.0133, D_LB -0.0658, ratio +0.41488) is the one this workspace's accepted row 711c4bf8 and its predecessor a32131ff were scored on.
heuristics.extrapolation: Registered runs, per-seed values and registration hashes in proof.md (Section 9, Appendices P, Q, R.1): level -96.42816 (128 seeds), ratio +0.41488 (400 seeds), paired P1 difference R9 D = -0.0121, sd 0.1321, n = 36, D_LB = -0.0658 (declared), and the earlier A25 run on the window [0, 2^25) D = +0.0022, D_LB = -0.0345 (n = 76, reported). Every diagnostic 0.
heuristics.limitations: Three Monte-Carlo bounds (level, relaxation ratio, paired P1 difference), each by a rule registered before its run; joint confidence at least 97%% (union bound). The relaxation ratio (row-18 relation E18 = E17 not imposed) is measured on the A0 family and applied to the P1 family. The paired runs use the printed-cell event; their P1 pairs are drawn from the exact law of C1, C2, G on the window, not from claws of the procedure (F7 is the separate late word W7, as in the A0 runs). The complete event (about 2^-71 per good pair) is not observed by any organizer run. The relaxation ratio is measured on the A0 family and applied to the P1 family; the argument is that the relaxed cells (E17, E18) are read identically by both families and that the paired R9 run measures the family difference on the printed-cell event. This is the parent's premise, unchanged and unweakened here.

heuristics.statement: Group independence within a chaining value (the form of H5-group-independence of the accepted 44870635): good pairs of one chaining value that share no endpoint (a0 or u) are independent trials of the accepted event, each with probability q3r; good pairs sharing an endpoint form a group counted once. Consequence used: for a uniform chaining value, J (accepted good pairs over all 2^32 scan words) has E[J(J-1)] <= 2^-7.5 E[J].
heuristics.scope: The Bonferroni factor (1 - 2^-8.5) per chaining value. Lemma 4 (proof.md Section 7) derives E[X_j(X_j-1)]/E[X_j] <= E[J(J-1)]/E[J] exactly from the distinct scan words u0 + n with u0 uniform.
heuristics.extrapolation: Under the statement E[J(J-1)]/E[J] = q3r E[K(K-1)]/E[K] <= q3r E[K] x 1.246 = 2^-54.61, below 2^-7.5 by a factor 2^47.1 (K = good pairs per chaining value, E[K] = 2^16.47; 1.246 = the measured E[K^2]/E[K]^2 over 24 chaining values, proof.md Appendix H). Panel: 0 of 2,124 good pairs share an endpoint; C2|C1 and G|C1C2 binomial across chaining values; F7 overdispersed (it reads the chaining value). Registered test on components of the accepted event (proof.md Appendix H.2): Part B of the 10-17 registration, run unchanged on 10-21: the forced-bit events B_t = ((E_t^x & m_t) == v_t) of rows 17..21 (the value-only cells of E17..E21, rates 2^-7, 2^-7, 2^-3, 2^-5, 2^-4), computed on the real compressions of both members of every good pair, ONE = every good pair of one chaining value over all 2^32 scan words (17,576; the registered target 20,000 exceeds what the chaining value has), MANY = 100 good pairs of each of 200 chaining values (20,000), all re-verified by an independent rebuild (0 and 0 bad): against N p_t the largest |z| is 2.43 (ONE) and 1.58 (MANY); ONE against MANY on rates, |z| at most 1.57; dispersion of E19, E20, E21 across the 200 chaining values chi-square 205.2, 190.2, 193.3 on 199 dof (two-sided p 0.734, 0.680, 0.798). The registered ONE-against-MANY formula (n1 - n2)/sqrt(n1 + n2) assumes equal sizes; applied to the unequal sizes it gives |z| up to 3.77, which is the size difference, not dependence (Appendix H.2). No within-chaining-value dependence of these components is detected.
heuristics.limitations: Independence of the rows 17..37 event between good pairs of one chaining value is not testable at any sample size and is the premise. The registered Part B test covers the forced-bit components of rows 17..21 only, not the full rows 17..37 event; C1 clusters in scan order (u's high bits) and F7 varies with the chaining value; both are measured and enter the derivation as the spread factor.

heuristics.statement: The total computation spent to obtain the characteristic P8 of 1a695f0b (its signed-difference SAT sweep, coupling checks and estimators; failed and repeated runs included) is at most A_C = 2^78 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger: A_C = 2^78 is the largest allowance; it enters the claimed time and preprocessing (78.09276).
heuristics.extrapolation: The search for P8 was run by the author of 1a695f0b, whose published run log (38 solver runs, 230,183 s listed) and total (under 2^21 core-seconds) are quoted with their source hash in proof.md Appendix R.4: at our measured 3,797,484 SHA-256 compressions per second that is 2^43.61 units, 34.4 bits under A_C. Our own measurements of the same kind of computation (proof.md Appendix R.2): a 39-step characteristic derived from scratch with the public tool of [LLW24] in 2^36.04 units; a 38-step pair from the published cells in 2^34.09 units; published figures up to 2^39.15 units.
heuristics.limitations: A charged allowance (an upper bound charged in full): we did not rerun P8's search; its log is the author's, quoted. With A_C = 2^84 the claim would be 84.96832.

heuristics.statement: S (the dense part of P8's semi-free-start pair) is obtained at a total cost of at most A_S = 2^74 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (A_S = 2^74).
heuristics.extrapolation: The Step-1 solve was run by the author of 1a695f0b (coupling check 662 s, single-threaded, inside the quoted total under 2^21 core-seconds; proof.md Appendix R.4); our own 38-step pair search from the published cells took 2,852.83 CPU-seconds = 2^34.09 units (proof.md Appendix R.2), 39.9 bits under A_S. selftest checks that the transcribed pair S reproduces and passes every test of rows 16..21 with equal outputs.
heuristics.limitations: A charged allowance (an upper bound charged in full), not a measurement; its support is the author-reported core-seconds. The Step-1 peak memory, re-measured under a 2^28 cap at 2^27.7542 (377cb363), is below the online cell 2^28.01141, which is the claimed peak (H6).

heuristics.statement: All development computation of this package, whether or not the procedure reads its output (exhaustive passes, C ports, the q3 and ratio studies, the F7 measurement, checks, failed runs and reruns), is at most DEV = 2^70 target compressions, and DEV is charged in full in the time.
heuristics.scope: The development item of the ledger (DEV = 2^70 x C operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: Hardware envelope (the bound for this allowance): every code execution of the project (10-05 to 10-21) ran on a 24-thread workstation with one GPU, a 12-thread server and one 32-vCPU cloud machine: at most 68 threads and one GPU for 1.4688 x 10^6 s at 2^40 word operations per thread-second and 2^47 per GPU-second, below 2^68.11 operations = 2^56.7 compressions, under DEV by more than 2^13; the recorded development of the A0-variant line is in proof.md Appendix R.3.
heuristics.limitations: A charged allowance (an upper bound charged in full), not a measurement: the hardware envelope above is the bound; it rests on the project's machine list and dates, and is more than 2^13 below the charge.

heuristics.statement: The counted table is the seven-lane bucket table of Appendix A.15: 2^23 buckets, each one 256-bit word (2^28 bytes), holding seven 36-bit lanes = [1 filled bit][9-bit tag = F mod 512][26-bit index into the R = 9 window]. A bucket access is address add 1 + 256-bit load 1 = 2. The tag test per word is address 1, load 1, add 1, and 1, add 1, and 1, and 1 = 7 operations of the v5 primitive set, the last one the merge of the two windows' fail-planes with `and` (the windows are alternatives, so by De Morgan a lane is a candidate iff it passes either: claws/u carries the factor 40 = 20 heads x 2 windows; an `or` of the same planes would test the intersection and find no claw), with no fused AND-NOT (Appendix A.15.2: the bias 2^9 - w puts the field's carry in the lane's guard bit, a = r AND 0x1FA keeps exactly the bits the P1 variant forces, and (a + (2^9-1)) AND G is exactly G on a fail and 0 on a pass, the polarity being read off the guard bit; the NOT of the earlier draft is eliminated, not repriced); a match is resolved by halving to the lane (3 x (and 1 + compare-and-branch 2) = 9) and extracting the field (shift 1, and 1), its tag (shift 1) and index (and 1), forming a0 (or 1) and F (shift 1, or 1): 18 operations per match, plus the other window's lane at the same position when the first fails its own check (extract 2, index 1, a0 1, F 2 = 6; mean 3 per match, the worst case 6 in the maximum path); the fused mask says a position passed, not which window, and exactly one of the two can pass. The per-head charge is 17, executed and counted by experiments/p1claw38.py counted-head (17 and 0 mismatches on 3,666,432 (tag, window, lane) comparisons, 56,700 of them one-window-only and 224 both-window): two windows x (address 1, load 1, add 1, and 1, add 1, and 1, and 1) = 14, compare-and-branch 2, setup 1, with w = W mod 512 shared by all 20 heads (they are equal mod 2^13) and each head's bucket base one add. The straddle pass (tag - tag_target wraps into the next bucket, 5/512 of the window queries) costs 9 per lookup. The post-filter segments are 7, 22, 29 and 30 operations, work-counter adds included. Every work-counter add is 1 and is counted.
heuristics.scope: The counted operations of the online procedure (proof.md A.15.2-A.15.4): 215.990 per claw (scan, post-filters, build and reset, the table build amortised over 2^32 scan words) and 3,014 per step 3b, with the maximum path vmax = 3,790,234,189,826,803 charged as a bound, not as an expectation.
heuristics.extrapolation: run_claw counts every operation; selftest checks the counted run against the per-u charge of Section 5 at a table where the a0 offset does not fit the entry (ls = 14, aw = 16, two side bits); our C port's scan count 425.592 per u (before packed access and counters) matches the straight-line count at the parent's size.
heuristics.limitations: The ledger is an exact analytic count read from the code, not a measurement; it does not rely on the organizer runs' counted_ops (reduced size). The unit costs are the fb176310 convention; the bucket access sequence is the explicit list of proof.md A.15.2.

heuristics.statement: The counted memory cell is the maximum over the counted phases, and that maximum is the measured peak resident set of the online program: the 2^23-bucket table of 2^23 x 32 = 268,435,456 bytes = 2^28 plus the port's own resident overhead, measured by this workspace's full-scale C ports on the identical 2^28-byte allocation at 2^28.011402 = 270,565,376 bytes (264,224 KiB) and 2^28.008101 = 269,947,000 bytes (~263,620 KiB). The charged cell is 2^28.0115, the larger measurement rounded up. The cited characteristic's preprocessing cells (Step-1 solve 2^27.7542, signed search 2^27.92) are below 2^28.0115, so the table's cell is the maximum over the counted phases.
heuristics.scope: The memory metric and the scored sum 82.9731 + (28.0115 - 20) = 90.9846.
heuristics.extrapolation: Our C port of the claw at 2^25 slots loaded with the 2^26 candidates of window R = 9 ran with a peak resident set of 137,460 KiB = 140,759,040 bytes = 2^27.069 (ru_maxrss; four chaining values peak at 136,948 to 137,460 KiB). The Step-1 re-measurement is reports/receipts/r38-step1-stream.json (two runs, 48,984 and 49,228 KiB, CNF sha256 cc4670c3...); the signed-search re-measurement is reports/receipts/r38-signedsearch-round1-notp8.json (86,404 KiB) and reports/receipts/r38-signedsearch-seed1.log (81,608 KiB). Every development execution ran under address-space caps of at most 2^28 bytes (proof.md Appendix R.3).
heuristics.limitations: The charged 2^28.0115 figure is the measured peak of the online port on the 2^28-byte table; it is above the abstract table-plus-state enumeration because it includes host overhead. The measurement covers the build and the scan; the post-filters and step 3b allocate no table and are not part of that run. The receipts behind the two byte counts are workspace files and are outside this package by intake design, so their numbers are quoted in A.15.5.

heuristics.statement: The bucket table of Appendix A.15 is loaded with the 2^26 candidates of window R = 9 in the cyclic order i = (n + ROT) mod 2^26, one fresh uniform ROT per chaining value, and each of the 2^23 buckets keeps the first seven candidates that arrive. The retained set of a bucket is therefore a uniformly placed block of seven consecutive positions in that bucket's insertion list -- an arc of seven, not an arbitrary seven-element subset. The filled-lane count is E[min(Binomial(2^26, 2^-23), 7)] = 6.336269 (filled fraction 0.905181) and the claw rate is claws/u = 40 x 6.336269 x 4/512 = 1.980084. Candidates that arrive after a bucket is full are dropped and pay the same build charge.
heuristics.scope: The claw rate 1.980084 per u (hence wbar, V_MAX and the success bound of A.15.4) and the match rate 40 x 6.336269 x 4/512 x 18. It claims no uniform seven-element subset, and no number of the score conditions on which indices are retained.
heuristics.extrapolation: Retention depends on the bucket index and on the insertion position, never on the lane's tag F mod 512, so the tags of retained lanes are uniform; the arc structure lives in the indices. The ledger prints 6.33627 filled lanes against the formula at the full table; the organizer experiment p1-bucket-r38 checks the claws against an independent sorted search at 2^16 candidates over 2^23 buckets, and the workspace fixture dev/occupancy38.py sweeps the window and word width.
heuristics.limitations: The arc structure is not excluded from influencing which index values are retained, and no measurement here separates an arc of seven from a uniform seven-subset at the tag level. That distinction does not enter the filed cost, which uses only the filled-lane count and tag uniformity; it would enter any claim about per-index statistics of retained lanes.

restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; step 3b accepts a pair only if A34..A37, E34..E37 of both members are equal, so every output is a collision (Lemma 1, proof.md Section 1).

Algorithm (proof.md Section 2, Appendix A.15; experiments/p1claw38.py): per chaining value a bucket table of 2^23 buckets, each one 256-bit word holding seven 36-bit lanes = [1 filled bit][9-bit tag][26-bit index], loaded with the 2^26 candidates a0 = (9<<26)|i of the window R = 9 in a random cyclic order, first seven per bucket (E[filled lanes] = 6.33627). The scan tests the 20 row-16 heads x 2 windows against the tag; a lane matches iff tag - tag_target is in {0,1,4,5}, the four values of F that differ from the target on bits 0 and 2 (the P1 variant's free bits), with a straddle pass into bucket + 1 when the difference wraps; the matching lane is resolved, a0 and F are formed, and the post-filters C1, C2, G, F7 and step 3b run exactly as in Section 3. The claw set is identical to the packed-slot machine's (selftest: claws = reference, every claw a true row-16 pass).

Cost: the procedure scans 2^32 distinct words u = u0 + n (mod 2^32) per chaining value; N_CV = 13,597,014,839,865,666 chaining values, each with one compression C = 2,728, cv_begin 75, the table reset (2^23 x 5) and the 2^26-candidate build (2^26 x 42). The mean online work of one chaining value is wbar = 1,839,727,753,105 word operations (per u: fixed 22, 20 heads x 17, straddle 3.52, matches x 21 (the match 18 plus the mean 3 of the second window's lane read), claws x (post-filter segments + q_pf x step 3b) = 427.679; claws per u 1.98008; 215.990 operations per claw). The cap V_MAX = 25,015,187,255,920,515,526,526,368,817 word operations is charged in full and the allowances A_C = 2^78 C, A_S = 2^74 C, DEV = 2^70 C are inside it (3.515%); with the overshoot and the final verification N = 25,894,425,781,903,873,524,473,417,044, and time_log2 = log2(N/2,728) = 82.97300 target compressions.

Success probability at least 0.39 under H1 (independent uniform chaining values), H1-P1 (q_pf = 2^-16.1877 for claws), H2-P1 (q3r >= 2^-71.4010 per good pair: the registered q3_model 2^-96.0133 plus the registered paired P1-vs-A0 lower bound -0.0658, measured on window R = 9, the only window this filing loads) and H3-P1 (group independence within a chaining value, giving E[J(J-1)] <= 2^-7.5 E[J]); Lemma 4 reduces the within-chaining-value term to H3-P1 exactly; Bonferroni per chaining value, independence across them, and Bernstein's inequality for the cap (Lemma 3).

Memory: 2^28.0115 bytes = 270,565,376 bytes (the 2^23-bucket table of 2^28 bytes plus the port's measured resident overhead, the larger of the two full-scale receipts), the maximum over the counted phases (H6).
